title.narrative: Promoting Food Security Among Drought Stricken Households in Samburu County

description.narrative: More than 200,000 persons in Samburu County are experiencing extreme water shortages with most of the water points drying. According to NDMA drought bulletin for the month of September 2022, vegetation greenness in Samburu County has remained below the average since the beginning of the year across the livelihood zones. The situation has exposed many families to hunger and starvation. This has been the case too for livestock which is the main source of income for the pastoralist communities in the county. The situation has worsened with a number of deaths (human) being reported from Samburu East and Samburu North sub-counties. The most affected villages are concentrated in Samburu East and Samburu North sub-counties mostly Nachola, El barta, Ndoto, Suguta Mar Mar, Wamba East, Uaso, Baawa , Wamba North, Wamba East wards and the borders between Samburu, Marsabit, Isiolo, Turkana and Baringo counties. The county government, through the department of special programmes and other stakeholders including Caritas Maralal, have since employed a number of interventions especially food drives targeting the most vulnerable households, but the situation is worsening as a result of the drought and insecurity arising from the same. The situation has forced pastoralists from the entire county to migrate with their livestock to neighbouring counties, especially Laikipia county, in search of water and pasture. The migration has consequently brought about tribal clashes with a number of people losing their lives from the clashes. Vulnerable groups in these communities, such as women, children, elderly and young Morans who take care of livestock and households have since been weakened due to lack of food and water among other basic services. The project will target the most vulnerable households (250 HHs) in Terter and Keleswa villages of Samburu North sub-county with relief food
